newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares end on high note, mood positive.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares end on high note, mood positive.

text.p: Shares ended with sharp gains, with several leading stocks touching fresh peaks. Traders said that the market could continue to advance on Thursday providing the foreign mood remains good.
*Total cash volume reached 26 billion escudos as the PSI index rose 1.21 percent to 7,877.16.

*Banco Espirito Santo rose 2.7 percent to 4,620 escudos in continuing reaction to the bank's first half results which were at the top of analysts' forecasts. Some traders see the stock targetting 4,700 escudos. "Non-residents were the most active buyers of BES today," said one trader.

*Banco Comercial Portugues also gained 1.9 percent after posting its results on Tuesday night. It closed at 3,453, slightly above the 3,450 that some traders had seen as a difficult barrier to break convincingly.

*"BCP was pushed to 3,453 escudos right at the end on just 100 shares. I am not sure whether that means the barrier is broken," said one trader. The average price of the stock during the session was 3,440 escudos.
*Cement firm Cimpor and engineering concern Efacec were other stocks to hit highs.
*Inparsa and its wood products subsidiary Sonae Industria were amongst the biggest gainers, with the former rising just over 10 percent.

*Explanations ranged from the possibility of Inparsa becoming the holding for the mobile phone business if the Sonae group and its allies wins the third concession due to be decided in the autumn to the good prospects for the wood business. Some traders said however the gains may be overdone. Inparsa has risen 90 percent since the start of June.
*On Thursday, Sonae and its allies will formally present their proposal for the third cellular phone licence at 1530 GMT in Oporto.
